chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Tirbal said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with a single divorce before consummating the marriage, and he gave testimony and informed her. He said: 'She has become permanently divorced from him at the moment he divorced her, and she is one of the women who are permanently divorced.'

I said: 'If he married her again and then divorced her with another single divorce before consummating the marriage?' He said: 'She has become permanently divorced from him at the moment he divorced her.'

I said: 'If he married her immediately again and then divorced her with a single divorce?' He said: 'She has become permanently divorced from him, and she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.'

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: She has become permanently divorced from him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man divorces his wife before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific ruling for a single divorce (*taliqah*) occurring before consummation (*dakhul*), establishing that it triggers a permanent separation (*banan*) rather than the standard revocable status. Unlike the general rule in Surah Al-Baqarah which requires two divorces before the finality, this narration indicates that a pre-consummation divorce is treated with the gravity of a final divorce, necessitating a new marriage to another man before she can return to the first husband. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the legal weight of the divorce act itself when consummation has not yet occurred.
